headlines: US 30-year Treasury auction cleared at 5.618%, in line with secondary market (per Stocktwits post)
Stocktwits chatter blames today's selloff on a report that OpenAI's annualised revenue is about $50B, not the $70B earlier reported (unconfirmed here)

rumors.text: OpenAI told investors annualised revenue was near $50B at end of September, about $20B below the $70B reported by FT and others
rumors.why: A revenue shortfall at OpenAI would hit AI-capex and AI-cloud names and could weigh on the index

rumors.text: CoreWeave's $2.6B AI loan reportedly has terms where uptime failures could force early debt paydowns
rumors.why: Tighter lender terms add financing risk for AI-cloud and data-center names

rumors.text: 30-year auction at 5.618% matched the secondary market, but stocks did not rally after it the way they did after yesterday's 10-year
rumors.why: Long yields near multi-year highs keep pressure on equity valuations
A crypto drop would add to risk-off tone, and miners are already down 6-11%

plays.reason: Selling accelerated into late morning on AI-revenue worries and no relief after the 30-year auction; QQQ weaker than SPY
plays.catalyst: OpenAI revenue shortfall chatter, long yields near highs

readings.whats_new: The selloff deepened: SPY is about 772 (-0.65%) versus 774.5 an hour ago and QQQ is down about 1.5%. The 30-year auction passed without a relief rally, and chatter now blames a report that OpenAI revenue is about $20B lower than earlier reported. AI-cloud and miner names (CRWV, CIFR, IREN, WULF, APLD) fell 4-11% while GME rose 4%; the Stocktwits crowd remains tagged bullish even as posts turn to panic.
